beats.headline: Doctor Hu, and the Crawler Project
beats.text: Carl needs the whole of it, so I give it to him in order. Doctor Hu. The Crawler Project. How fifty thousand of us came to be standing under the Princess Posse's banner. None of it is anything he would ever have been told from inside; that is the thing about being retired, you learn what the ones still crawling are not shown. He listens. That is rarer than it sounds.

beats.headline: Blood bar rules are back
beats.text: The blood bar rules are back in force inside the safe rooms. I tell Carl now, while knowing it still costs nothing. Around us the NPCs, the mercenaries and the rest of us former crawlers are building the defences on the same line, three kinds of people this format has always kept apart, working shoulder to shoulder. I do not have a rule for that. I am watching it closely.

beats.headline: The necklace is worse
beats.text: The orc on the yak is the king, not his son. Nobody tell Rosetta he is here yet. I will tell her. She has history with him. Carl asks how he levelled so fast. A Ring of Divine Suffering for the stats, and a necklace of Indelible Woe for the spells. It trades out one of your spells for one of a crawler's; kill them and it is one of their five highest. It fell out of use because combatants were farming crawlers to power it. Carl asks if the ring is any better. The necklace is worse. Much worse.

beats.headline: Who are you?
beats.text: A man is heading for the saferoom door, and I put my hand on his shoulder. Excuse me. Carl? Can you tell me something? Who are you, and where are we? The last thing I remember is my last day as a game guide. A woman named Rosetta says my brain was scrambled in my crawl, that I went into debt to the Viceroys to fix it, and that the blast ruined the repairs. I sit and look at my hands. I thought I was done. I thought I was going home. I lost my key.

beats.headline: He sings to find the guild
beats.text: Carl slides in next to me at the bar, and I bring up the war mages. Under normal circumstances any of this earns a beating from the AI and the showrunners. I watched Herot's season as a game guide; trust what that little lizard says, find a way to talk to them directly. War mages will use you and kill you. Shadow mimics are the real problem. Then I take the stage in the Lollipop and sing Love Shack, badly. A gauge appears over me. The guild is here. The needle never leaves the red.

beats.headline: Do not kill the shells
beats.text: An apartment. Human Shells inside it, and one of them wears the name of Louis's mother. Carl and Donut are about to do the obvious thing and I stop them. Do not kill the shells. We had them in my season; they will be filled with something else. The AI is explicit about what this is: every apartment on this course is a what-if, built around a crawler it finds interesting. You do not put a blade into a what-if. You walk through it, and you keep walking.

beats.headline: It works like an inventory
beats.text: Carl asks how Herot could pull someone out of the holding area. I spent a season on a site-prep crew. It works almost like an inventory: whoever is designing the floor selects the stored individual from a menu and places them. A simple procedure. Nobody looks at that catchall area once a season starts, because nobody ever goes into it. It was built as a backup for the Nothing, which was meant to catch problem entities and be forgotten about. The backup became redundant.

beats.headline: Out of the driver's seat
beats.text: Carl stamps on the roof. I tell him I am not leaving the wheel. He needs a more reliable driver for this. He tells me my story isn't done and to get to the RV. The sluggalos tell me to get out of their chair. I get out. I go to the RV. Behind me the deep fryer comes on. That is not in the plan.
